# Generator assumptions — Cascadia Revenue Assurance

> **Synthetic data from a seeded generator (seed 20260911). Simulated: not a real company, customer, partner, product or book of business.** Every customer, partner, subscription and transaction below was invented by this script from a fixed seed. No figure in this module may be read as a claim about any real book of business. Any resemblance to a real company, partner or person is unintended.

## What the generator does, and does not, decide

The generator simulates **customer intent** and emits **order transactions**. It tracks the register — the last quantity each customer asked for, and whether they cancelled — because a customer who adds licences is adding to what they last asked for. It never computes an effective quantity, a term boundary, a proration, or an accepted/rejected flag. Those belong to the engines and to `governance/entitlement-rules.md`. When the generator emits a transaction the rules will refuse, it does so deliberately, and it records only the *count* it intended, by reason, in `data/raw/manifest.json`, so `src/validate.py` can check that the engine refused exactly those.

## Realised movement beside the designed band

Rates are per **active subscription-month** — one roll per subscription per calendar month in which it was open and not yet cancelled. There were **48,429** such rolls.

| Outcome | Designed | Realised count | Realised rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `ADD` | 3.0% | 1,417 | 2.93% |
| `REDUCE` | 2.0% | 929 | 1.92% |
| `CANCEL` | 1.0% | 491 | 1.01% |
| `REJECT` | 0.5% | 259 | 0.53% |

`REDUCE` realises slightly under design because a subscription at one licence cannot reduce and stays flat instead. Refused transactions are counted here by the generator's intent; the engine's own classification is in `fact_order_event` and the two are reconciled by `src/validate.py`.

Refused transactions intended, by reason: `ADD_AFTER_CANCEL` 5, `DUPLICATE_CANCEL` 1, `DUPLICATE_NEW` 39, `NOOP_QUANTITY` 116, `REDUCE_AFTER_CANCEL` 2, `REDUCE_TO_ZERO` 54, `UNKNOWN_SUBSCRIPTION` 42.

## Parameter block

Every tunable assumption, as set for this run. These are arbitrary and are disclosed rather than defended.

| Parameter | Value | What it controls |
|---|---|---|
| `SEED` | 20260911 | Fixed seed; the same seed reproduces byte-identical files |
| `WINDOW_START` / `WINDOW_END` | 2024-07-01 / 2026-06-30 | Openings and transactions fall inside this window |
| `AS_OF` | 2026-06-30 | The date every measure is stated at |
| `N_CUSTOMERS` / `N_DIRECT` | 4,000 / 200 | Size of the book; Direct is the small, large-licence channel |
| `PARTNERS` shares | 55% / 30% / 15% | Unequal partner shares of the Partner customers |
| `P_ANNUAL` | 60% | Share of subscriptions on an annual term |
| `P_SECOND_SUBSCRIPTION` | 10% | Customers who open a second subscription at least 30 days later |
| `PARTNER_QTY` | median 8, sigma 0.9, clamp (1, 80) | Opening licence count, Partner (log-normal) |
| `DIRECT_QTY` | median 200, sigma 0.7, clamp (25, 2000) | Opening licence count, Direct (log-normal) |
| `P_ADD` / `P_REDUCE` / `P_CANCEL` / `P_REJECT` | 3.0% / 2.0% / 1.0% / 0.5% | Per active subscription-month; the rest flat |
| `ADD_UPLIFT` | (1.1, 1.6) | An `ADD` asks for the register times this, at least +1 |
| `REDUCE_FACTOR` | (0.4, 0.9) | A `REDUCE` asks for the register times this, at least 1, always below the register |
| `REJECT_MIX_ACTIVE` | {'NOOP_QUANTITY': 0.45, 'REDUCE_TO_ZERO': 0.25, 'DUPLICATE_NEW': 0.15, 'UNKNOWN_SUBSCRIPTION': 0.15} | Which refusal an active subscription attracts |
| `REJECT_MIX_CANCELLED` | {'ADD_AFTER_CANCEL': 0.4, 'REDUCE_AFTER_CANCEL': 0.4, 'DUPLICATE_CANCEL': 0.2} | Which refusal a recently cancelled subscription attracts |
| `AFTER_CANCEL_MONTHS` | 3 | How many months after a cancel a key still attracts refusals |
| `UNKNOWN_KEY_BASE` | 90000 | Subscription numbers from here up are never issued; an `UNKNOWN_SUBSCRIPTION` names one |

## Why the shape is what it is

- **Openings are uniform across the whole window**, as the brief asked, so annual renewals occur inside it for roughly half the annual book and the other half is still in its first term at the as-of date. No opening book was front-loaded; that would have been an assumption the brief did not make.
- **An `ADD` is sized against the register**, because the register is what the customer believes they have. When a reduction is pending, an add can therefore land between the register and the effective quantity; rule 4.2 in the rules document says what happens then, and G13 tests it.
- **A `CANCEL` sets the register quantity to 0** on the day it is received. The subscription stays billable to term end. That is the module's largest single source of gap and it is a consequence of the rules, not of the generator.
- **Nothing here is drawn from, calibrated to, or shaped after any real company's data.** The parameters were chosen to make the rules' consequences visible, and are disclosed for that reason.
